The letter opens in clear and changes to cipher mid-sentence: fr. 3984 f. 145, the head of the letter: the clear opening, then the cipher, with three-letter word codes ( xen , pra , rom , mon , dur , hes ) among the numbers. Image: Bibliothèque nationale de France, fr. 3984 f. 145 (canvas 268), via Gallica. This leaf is in a different cipher, the Feria–Mansfeld key, whose numbering is unrelated: ba 24, ca 25, da 10, la 59, ma 49, que 66, and de the single figure 8. Satoshi Tomokiyo’s page on the ciphers of Philip II’s reign carries, as an image, a Syllabic cipher for Duke of Feria and Count of Mansfeld (1593) , cited at fr. 3984 ff. 130 and 145. This leaf bears it out: its values run far higher than in the office cipher of 1592–93 (97, 98, 800, 7243), and it carries the three-letter word codes he describes ( pra, rom, mon, xen, vul, cil ; he gives vas = segnor as an example). All twenty cipher lines were transcribed on 5 October 2026: 598 groups. Decoded with his table, they give Spanish: a mi no me parece que puede , se [ha] de poner todo lo que se puede , lo que podemos , aliento, y si ella apareciera, y palabra , no estamos desesperados , peligro , espero , de acudir a lo que esta , pareceria que venia a ayudar … y la cavalleria , a lo menos no parece sino . A Spanish character model of the period scores the decode at −2.500 per character; 200 keys with the same values shuffled among the numbers score at most −3.378. A free hill-climb over all numbers collapses onto que and was rejected; a constrained search for the numbers missing from the table fixed 57 = li ( peligro , aliento ). 64, probably ha by context, is not separated from na by the model and stays open. Scored line by line for sense, 224 of the 598 groups (37.5%) give Spanish. The diacritic finals and doubling marks were left out of the transcription, so the words come out without their final consonant. Phrases scattered among unread word codes do not make sentences: read as a text, the letter is decoded, not read (reading audit, 22 October 2026), and the 37.5% is withdrawn as a reading figure.
ibarra1593.html#crib

The other folio Tomokiyo cites for this key was opened on 23 October 2026. F. 130 is a letter of Mansfeld to Feria, Formentieres, 7 July 1593, wholly in this cipher, and f. 131r–v holds its contemporary French decipherment, together with that of Feria’s own letter of 10 July (cipher f. 143). The crib fixes 64 = ha , 63 = he , 62 = hi , 31 = jo , 19 = fa , 81 = vi , and the word codes xen = Infanteria, pun = hombre, mon = gente, tel = exercito, fon = Flandes, dir = Magestad, Vas = señor ( mon and tel flagged for review). With them about a quarter of the letter’s sentences build; the partial reading is texts/no68_reading_b28.md (three-letter codes still open in angle brackets, [?word] doubtful): A mi no me parece que puede con esta gente la [?tregua], me parece la que <gar> en <sil> de <vis> <77> de <cle> que puede ha[?…] y que <var> es to[?…]. No estamos desesperados de [?presente] <bel> de <pus>, solo nos de <77> ta de todas estas <vel>; el peligro que en ta <vir> <xur>, espero en Dios que ha de acudir a lo que esta[?…] de su <vis> [?…] poco <ful> <xas> <cel> lo que <pra> di[?…] <xur>. The letter stays decoded, not read: the other three-letter groups ( pra , xur , gar , dur , var , tor , vis …) carry much of the sense, and the 1593 French decipherer left them blank too.

The three-letter word codes other than those the f. 131 decipherment fixes ( pra, dur, hes, gar, rom, vul, cil, var, vis, tor, xur … ), which Tomokiyo does not tabulate and the decipherer of 1593 also left blank. The nearest candidate list, fr. 3995 f. 101 beside the Spanish office key, is an Italian nomenclature of another correspondence. Catalogued as a letter of the French marshals to the King dated 1520 (BnF fr. 3081 f. 41, DECODE R2322), the two cipher pages are a copy of the articles Cardinal Campeggio swore to the cardinals Bourbon, Lorraine and Tournon: if elected pope, he would work for the return of Milan, Asti and Genoa to Francis I. George Lasry recovered the key and deciphered the first page in 2022. His key was applied here to the second page, which had no published decipherment, with five small corrections; all but one symbol and one code group are decrypted. DECODE R2322 carries four images from Gallica: f. 41r and f. 41v in cipher, f. 42r blank, and on f. 42v the endorsement. The cipher is a homophonic substitution with invented signs and no word division. It has 20 letters with one to four signs each, plus signs for CON and ET. Lasry found that the same key also decrypts BnF Dupuy 265 f. 132, a letter of the bishop of Mâcon to the King of 29 May 1535. Mâcon was then ambassador in Rome. On f. 41v the key needed a few adjustments: The three-stroke sign that Lasry lists third under H stands for Y : roy, iceluy, quoy, veoyant, moyennant. The “Rg” sign is P , not T: penser, pourveoir, pouvoir, partie, persuasion. A looped “4” stands for R : pour, pourveoir. Lasry’s first “unknown” sign, a bold ʃ, is probably S : “par [s]es dictes persuasions”. His second “unknown”, a cluster of strokes, occurs once, in “devers [·] et ses successeurs”. It is probably a code for the Emperor (grade M).

Lasry’s decipherment of f. 41r was published only as red overlays on three crops of the page. On 23 October 2026 it was transcribed letter by letter from those crops and checked against the figures of the DECODE image at seven places: one overlay letter was corrected (l. 7, “par armes”), two were confirmed on the figures (l. 22 “pacificque”, l. 28 “si esplore”), and one look-alike in l. 1 is left as a hole ( texts/f41r_reading.md , with English). Spelling is the figures’; word division and punctuation are added. The page opens: Articles iures par monsieur le cardinal Campege es mains de messeigneurs les cardinaulx de Bourgon, Loraine et Tornon. Aiant moi, Laurens cardinal de Campege, [?par] longue experience cogneu quant de doumage a porte a la crestiente, et mesmement au siege apostolicque, la disention des princes crestiens, nee par divers desirs de augmenter leur seigneurie et dition. Campeggio recalls the wars among Christian princes, which brought the Holy See and Christendom almost to the end; he has worked for a more stable and universal peace, so that Christendom might recover the provinces held by the infidels, fight “le grant Thurc” and root out the heresies of “ce temps si esplore et calamiteulx”. None of this can be done without the counsel, help and power of the Most Christian King. The sentence runs on to f. 41v.

[brackets] are restorations or a code group, and … marks short gaps. … [tres chre]stien et serenissime seigneur Francois roy de France, la Maieste duquel a esté souventefois recherchée de contribuer a l’entreprinse de l’expedition contre iceluy grant Turc, qu’il a tousiours niée, le pouvant faire sinon que premier sa Maieste feust reintegrée et restituée en la duché de Milan, conté d’Ast et seigneurie de Gennes, desquels en avoit esté spoliée violentement et par force. Et pendant que sa Maieste n’estoit reintegrée en ses seigneuries, ne povoit pencer a une expedition si loingtaine ne aux chouses oc[c]upées d’iceluy grant Thurc. Par quoy, veoyant la volunté et grande envie dudit treschrestien roy n’estre si loing des armes qu’il ne les puisse reprendre, en maniere que la paix, qui n’a aucun lien ferme, … soit pour engendrer bien toust et prestement en Italie aultre plus grande fla[m]e de guerre que devant; si moyennant l[e]s … l’on ne vient a penser d’y pourveoir, ce que par grande experience se cognoist ne pouvoir faire sans contenter en quelque partie le dit tres crestien roi. Et pour ce, s’il plaist a Dieu me donner grace d’estre pape, suis venu avecques les negotiateurs de Sa Maieste aux articles ci souscripts et aux conventions par moy iurees. Et premierement ie [s]aierai avecques toute demonstration, persuasion et exhortation que l’on pourroit user, ainsi devers [code: the Emperor?] et ses successeurs comme vers les detenteurs du duche de Milan et tout l’estat du dit duche, conte d’Ast et seigneurie de Gennes, que les dicts estatz et seigneuries soient rendus et restitues es mains du dit seigneur roi tres crestien ou des illustrissimes seigneurs ses enfans et successeurs. Et quant par ses dictes persuasions et voie … Translation. The Most Christian King has often been asked to join the expedition against the Turk. He has always refused unless he were first restored to the duchy of Milan, the county of Asti and the lordship of Genoa, which were taken from him by force. Unless that is provided for, the peace, which has no firm bond, will soon kindle a greater war in Italy than before. So the cardinal, if God gives him the grace to become pope, has agreed with the King’s negotiators to the articles below and sworn to them. First, he will use every persuasion with the Emperor(?) and with the holders of Milan to have Milan, Asti and Genoa returned to the King or to his sons. The page ends in the middle of the second clause.

The DECODE images were fetched with the project’s login. Two Claude subagents transcribed f. 41v sign by sign, one taking lines 1–19 and the other lines 20–37. They used Lasry’s key table and his red overlays on f. 41r as a reference for this scribe’s hand, then decrypted the transcription with the key. The adjustments in section 01 came from words that repeat across the page. The line-by-line transcriptions are in the repository folder.

Two further passes settled every doubtful place but two. In l. 12 the group after “chouses” is OCVPEES, “oc[c]upées” (C). In l. 15 a sign first taken for E is Lasry’s second M sign: “des armes” (C). Counted on the transcription, 1,339 of the page’s 1,341 letter tokens have a value (99.9%). One symbol in l. 19 is outside the key. “fla[m]e” is from context (grade C). The code cluster taken as the Emperor rests on context only (grade M). The value S for Lasry’s ʃ sign is grade C. The scribe wrote one A twice in l. 16. f. 41r, l. 1: “[?par]” rests on a look-alike sign (the figures give D, the look-alike of P). The rest of the articles are missing: f. 41v breaks off and f. 42 is blank but for the endorsement. The endorsement’s “marechaulx” does not fit the content, and the date of 1534 rests on the three cardinals named. Neither has been checked against a history of the 1534 conclave.

Same holes. Articles sworn by my lord Cardinal Campeggio into the hands of my lords the Cardinals of Bourbon, Lorraine and Tournon. I, Lorenzo, Cardinal Campeggio, having learnt [?by] long experience how much harm the discord of the Christian princes, born of their various desires to enlarge their lordship and dominion, has brought to Christendom, and above all to the Apostolic See: as each has sought to overpower the other by arms and each to defend his own, it has come to war and to arms among Christians, cruelly, for many years. And some of the past popes have been forced to undergo and enter into the same danger and expense of war, so far that the Apostolic See [sic: repeated] and Christendom were almost brought low to the very end. Having many times striven against this covetousness, with those officers to whom it belonged, being about divers princes, I have put all my study into raising and settling among them a more stable and universal peace, so that, Christendom remaining at peace and the princes content within their borders, it might think of recovering so many provinces occupied by the infidels, and of subduing and fighting the common enemy of our faith, the Great Turk, and of rooting out the many heresies that run in these times so woeful and calamitous. Which things, so very hard and difficult, cannot be done, not to say thought of, without the good counsel, help and power of the most Chris[tian] king (continues on f. 41v: "... and most serene lord Francis, King of France, whose Majesty has often been asked to contribute to the enterprise of the expedition against the said Great Turk ...") f. 41v Francis I refuses to join a crusade against the Turk until Milan, Asti and Genoa are restored to him; Cardinal Campeggio swears that, if elected pope, he will press the Emperor and the holders of Milan to return them. Tournon became a cardinal in 1530 and Campeggio died in 1539, so these are articles for the conclave of October 1534; the page breaks off mid-sentence. A letter of clear French with 26 cipher runs, probably from Henri, duc de Guise, to his cousin Mercœur (BnF fr. 15564 f. 78). George Lasry recovered the key in 2022 but published only the decipherment of f. 27. His key was applied to a new transcription and extended by about fifteen values: 983 of 998 cipher signs decrypt to sense. ʃʃn → PAR · ɛ = F · :: = H · ∽ = G · gb = MONSIEUR · L’ACCOMMODER PAR LA DOUCEUR [Guise] → the duc de Mercœur · homophonic cipher with a small nomenclator · 16 April 1587 Guise to the Duke of Mercœur, 16 April 1587 from Henri, duc de Guise → to Duc de Mercœur Go to the full text ↓ BnF français 15564 f. 78 (DECODE R4158): one page of clear French with 26 cipher runs. It was decrypted with the key George Lasry recovered in 2022. Lasry lists f. 78 among the letters he solved but did not publish its decipherment. Daniel Bourdeau · posted 22 September 2026 · updated 26 October 2026 Method: read with known key · Extent: partial (98% of the cipher) Credits · George Lasry (key or decipherment used) known key At a glance Known key applied · partial (98% of the cipher) The letter A letter of 16 April 1587 (“Ce xvj Avril 1587”), probably from Henri, duc de Guise, to his Lorraine cousin Mercœur. It speaks of “mon frere” and Bellièvre. Where BnF fr. 15564 f. 78, DECODE R4158. The catalogue listed three records here as an unknown sender to Mercœur, 1587, none decrypted. The cipher A French cipher with code groups, the same as f. 27 (R4155), which George Lasry deciphered in 2022. How it was read Lasry says he solved f. 78 but did not publish it. Every sign was transcribed and decrypted with his key, which fits unchanged. A French language model chose between ambiguous key values, and three passes against the images added about fifteen values. What it says The writer asks Mercœur to delay his decision a few days until his brother can take the place once Bellièvre arrives. He also discusses the levy of reiters and a lady who meddles in affairs. Still open Three code groups and twelve signs. Credit Lasry’s key and his f. 27 decipherment are on Satoshi Tomokiyo’s Cryptiana. f. 151 (R4167) is a different cipher, closed as too short in a separate write-up.

Je tiens tousjours certaine la levee de Reistres que l’on me mande estre [QUE/POUR LE?] 12 N(?), et qu’il y a quelque asseurance de la part de la Royne d’Angleterre qu’elle n’en tirera(?) de France. Mais je [voy?] le peu d’apparance qu’il y a que telles gens voulsissent arrester leur sejour en ung pays si sterile, duquel ilz ont tesmoigne les incommoditez, VEU MESMES QUE LA CAVALLERIE ET LES TROUPES AU [code: DUC] DE PARME NE PEUVENT VIVRE NI DEMEURER, ESTANS QUE CETTE OCCASION FORT DESBANDEES. JE(?) TIENS QUE CERTAIN POUR LEUR BUT ET RETRAICTE, ET PRESTS TOUSIOURS EN P[?] ET SUR NOUS; ET EST PLUS IMPORTANT QUE JAMAIS DE RESOUDRE L’ESTAT DE NOS AFFAIRES ET [??] EMPESCHER LE PASSAGE, ET REPOULSER CE[T ORAGE?] A QUOY NOUS AVONS TOUS PARTICULIER INTEREST, MONSIEUR. Je trouve tres bon vostre advis que le faict de 23(?), et suis bien d’opinion qu’il seroit fort a propos de L’ACCOMMODER PAR LA DOUCEUR, en ayant escrit a MONSIEUR DE [code 8ı] que [..] massieur(?) de faire en cela ce que nous luy conseillerons. Mais il faut que je vous die librement qu’il A UNE DAME(?) QUI AVEC [PEU DE?] PRUDENCE S’EN EST LE TROP AVANT DES AFFAIRES, AYANT ESTE SI MAL ADVISEE DE VOULOIR PERSUADER A SON MARI QUE SON FRERE ET NOUS NE RECHERCHONS QUE SON CONTENTEMENT PARTICULIER [?] SON DESAVANTAGE, voulant tirer le payement de ses pensions et assignations PAR LA REDDITION DES PLACES. Je suis a la verité honteux(?) de vous parler de cette particularité, mais estans d’une mesme maison cette liberté nous doibt estre permise, d’estimant(?) qu’une(?) lettre de vous a MONSIEUR DE [code 8ı], AVEC CONSEIL DE CE QUE [code: VOUS?] JUGEREZ A PROPOS, QUE LE BIEN GENERAL EN SERVIRA DE BEAUCOUP. Et vous supplie tres humblement luy en vouloir escrire librement, et vous baise tres humblement les mains. Ce xvj Avril 1587. In English, in outline: the writer is glad that “their” advice agrees that the troubles make Mercœur’s presence in his government of Brittany necessary, since the people there fear being abandoned. He asks Mercœur to delay his decision a few days, until his brother can go and take the place once Bellièvre has arrived. The reiter levy is certain, and there is some assurance from the Queen of England. In cipher: the Duke of Parma’s cavalry and troops cannot stay, and it is more important than ever to settle “our affairs” and stop the passage. The matter of “23” should be settled “par la douceur”. A lady has meddled too far in affairs and has persuaded her husband that “his brother and we” seek only his own interest, to his cost. He wants his pensions paid “par la reddition des places”. A letter from Mercœur to “Monsieur de [8ı]” would serve the common good.

Cryptiana’s GL.htm (“Duke of Guise? in BnF fr.15564”) gives Lasry’s 2022 key table and his decipherment of f. 27, and says he solved ff. 27, 78, 119 and 142. The DECODE images of R4155, R4158, R4167 and neighbouring records were downloaded. The f. 27 overlay was used to calibrate the sign shapes against Lasry’s table. Every sign of f. 78 was labelled, one line per cipher run: 952 labels, with each nomenclator group as one label (998 signs when group members are counted singly). Where a label had more than one key value, a French letter model of about 1600 (5-grams) chose among them. A stricter solver (simulated annealing) that forced one value per label merged distinct homophones and gave worse text, so it was set aside. Three sign-by-sign passes against native-resolution crops added values missing from Lasry’s sheet or wider than it: ɋ/ƀ = M, ɛ = F, ≈ʃ = P, the R shape = B, :: = H, ∽ = G, ∩ = Y, and the groups ʃʃɤ = MON, ʃbn = NOUS, gb = MONSIEUR, g2 = DUC.
mercoeur1587.html#what-stays-open

Three code groups that are not in the key, each used once: ʃʃ in run 3, ẜʃʃ in run 7, ≈ƀ in run 22. The guesses from context (MAIS, QUELQUE, PEU DE) are graded M. Twelve unresolved signs in runs 3, 17, 18 and 19 (“EN P[?]”, “[??] EMPESCHER”, “CE[T ORAGE?]”). They are legible, but no key value or French fits the letter count. Name codes in the clear text: 8ı (“Monsieur de …”), 23 and 12 N. Each occurs once or twice and is not on Lasry’s sheet. Together with the doubtful readings, these holes leave 92.1% of the words of the decrypted text read (measured 24 October 2026), under 95%. The sender is not named in the letter. Guise is the most likely writer (Tomokiyo: “probably from the Duke of Guise”), but that is an inference.

A letter of the Grand Marshal of the Crown in the Sanguszko archive, clear Polish and Latin with 232 cipher figures in 77 values, word-divided. Homophonic annealing with modern and period Polish models, cribs and a dictionary gave no stable key, and the same solver also fails a synthetic control of this size, so the result is inconclusive. Dukla → Jakub Dunin · numerical cipher, word-divided, Polish · 18 March 1714 · attempted, not solved Józef Mniszech to Jakub Dunin, 1714 from Józef Wandalin Mniszech A letter from the Grand Marshal of the Crown to the Crown regent, half clear Polish and Latin, half numbers; every attack tried here failed, and so did the same attack on a synthetic text of its size. Daniel Bourdeau · posted 14 October 2026 Method: not solved · Extent: text not obtained not solved At a glance Not solved · text not obtained The letter Józef Wandalin Mniszech, Grand Marshal of the Crown, to Jakub Dunin, Crown regent, from Dukla, 18 March 1714. Clear Polish with Latin phrases, the sensitive words in figures. Where Archiwum Narodowe w Krakowie, Archiwum Sanguszków, ASang_teka_290/6; DECODE R7524, catalogued with the date 16 March 1714. The cipher 232 figures from 12 to 157, 77 different values, written word by word with dots inside a word. Its design is not established. How it was tried Homophonic annealing with Polish language models, with and without word boundaries, cribs, a period dictionary, and the Sanguszko key records. No stable key. Why it resists 232 figures in 77 values is too little for the solver: a synthetic Polish text of the same size and design was recovered only to 21%. Still open The whole cipher. A stronger solver or more of Mniszech’s cipher letters is needed. This letter was filed in the Sanguszko archive, and on this site until 14 October 2026, with Barbara Potocka’s nine letters to the same Jakub Dunin; hers are in a different cipher, with their own page .

DECODE names the sender “Mniszech J[ózef], m[arszałek] w[ielki] k[oronny]”, the Grand Marshal of the Crown, and the receiver “Dunin Jakub, regent koronny”. The letter opens with eight lines of clear Polish, then alternates cipher words with clear Polish and Latin ones: praetextu consilii , congressow , generaliter , unanimi voto , Rempublicam , iest plus quam certum , correspondencye , tractantur . mniszech1714.html#cipher

Re-read at full resolution on 5 October 2026, the cipher has 53 words, 232 figures and 77 distinct values between 12 and 157. Dots join the figures of a word, a gap separates words, and an equals sign joins a word across a line end. Four words are a single figure (12, 38, 56, 133). Some words recur: 22.118.82.36.31.81 four times (twice followed by 17.68), 36.31.157.31.33.81.15.20 twice, 144.76.144 twice. Doubled figures occur (12.19.19.118, 27.28.28.119). These features would fit a homophonic letter cipher that keeps word division, but that design has not been shown. The system is not Barbara Potocka’s. Her alphabet runs 14–39 with doubled homophones (25 and 50 = e); shifted by −40 to +40 or scaled by 1 to 4 it fits nothing here.

23 September 2026: homophonic annealing scored with a Polish five-letter model (the shared pl-modern ), a tentative crib hetmanow , a hypothetical null 33 with 130 = ch , and a search penalised towards Polish letter frequencies. No coherent text. The crib values are not key material. The three key records of the Sanguszko collection on DECODE: R7515 (a numerical alphabet, a = 5/10/15, two series) and R7460/R7461 (graphic signs). None fits. 5 October 2026: annealing that uses the writer’s word boundaries, scored on pl-modern and on a period model built from Jan Chryzostom Pasek’s memoirs and Gutenberg Polish, with and without the cribs. No convergence. 5 October 2026: dictionary-word annealing over a 49,000-word list. 34–36 of the 53 words land in the dictionary, but every restart gives a different key: at 232 figures and 77 values the search is underdetermined.

A synthetic Polish homophonic text of the same length, 232 tokens, with a comparable alphabet (75 signs) was given to the same solver. It recovered 49 of 232 positions (21.1%). A solver that cannot break a known text of this size proves nothing about the letter: it does not show that the cipher is homophonic, or that it cannot be broken.

Fr. 3975 is a volume of the Nevers papers for 1587 in the Collection Mémoires de la Ligue , on Gallica as btv1b90605473 . The BnF’s piece-by-piece notice lists f. 28 as no. 7, “Lettre avec chiffrement et déchiffrement adressée à M. le duc de Nevers pour lui rendre compte d’un voyage à Lyon. Ce XXVII mars 1587” , and f. 30 as no. 8, “Lettre adressée par le même correspondant et sur le même sujet” , 4 April. Both are signed with the same monogram and written in a hand that fills its line ends with a long s. Nothing on the leaves says where the writer was. DECODE’s “Rome” seems to be borrowed from a neighbouring piece (no. 13, the marquis Malatesta, Di Roma ). f. 28r–v, 27 March (R4285): code numbers 94, 6 and 23, each followed by the key’s virgule, and a ten-symbol place name before the clear “ce xxvij Mars”. f. 30r, 4 April (R4286): code 45 and one run of thirteen symbols. A contemporary hand glossed the code and the first four symbols of the run. F. 30r. “45, a esté en tres grande alarme, passant pres”, then the run. The gloss Le duc d’Espernon is over 45, and Lyon is written small under the first four signs. Image: Bibliothèque nationale de France, fr. 3975 f. 30r, via Gallica (btv1b90605473). The key is no. 11 in Tomokiyo’s catalogue of the Nevers key book, BnF fr. 3995 f. 23 (Gallica btv1b525085665 , view 52). It has a homophonic alphabet of two to four symbols per letter, capitals for twenty-two small words (C = de, F = et, K = me, M = avec…), and some hundred names and words written as a figure or letter followed by a virgule. The instruction on the sheet: “L’on pourra se servir de toutes sortes de caractaires que l’on voudra faire a plaisir avec ceulx qui sont dans ce chiffre, lesquelz serviront de nulles” , so invented symbols are nulls. The name list leans south and to Auvergne: St Vidal, Mandelot, Maugiron, Randan, the grand prieur, the comte de Sault, the bishop of Clermont. The full table is in targets/nevers1587/key.md . BnF fr. 3995 f. 23, the alphabet of key no. 11 (turned). Under l: m and π; under y: ^ and <; under o: n, u and an underlined ꭓ; under p: a script l and a script F. Image: Bibliothèque nationale de France, fr. 3995 f. 23, via Gallica (btv1b525085665, view 52).

Applied directly from the table, the key decoded the codes and the glossed Lyon (π ^ ꭓ é = l y o n). The rest gave no sense: “… a p c e t a i s”, and a dateline of “r a q …”. Enumerating every value and null against a French language model, and allowing one or two scribal slips, produced nothing convincing. Tomokiyo notes that key no. 11 “is used in a letter of Cardinal of Guise to the Duke of Nevers, Clairmont, 25 February”, BnF fr. 3413 f. 102 (Gallica btv1b52510705j , view 213). It is not the cardinal’s. It has the same hand, the same long-s line fillers and the same monogram as the two letters in fr. 3975, and it is dated in clear “De Clairmont ce xxv feb” . It reports the Gevaudan Huguenots’ raids and the King’s order to St Vidal to prepare the sieges of Marvejols and Le Malzieu (Joyeuse took both in August 1586, so the letter is of February 1586). It has five lines of cipher with a decipherment written between them: “Mr du Mayne m’a mandé qu’il desire que je l’aille trouver avec ma compagnie, deux mille hommes de pied et bon nombre de ma cavalerie … si je l’abandonnois” . No name appears on the leaves. The three letters show a man who writes from Clermont and from Randan. He keeps a company and cavalry of his own, and Mayenne asks him to bring two thousand foot. He had asked the King for leave to keep horse against the Gevaudan Huguenots. He stays well clear of the queen of Navarre’s affairs, and he hopes to wait on Nevers at Nevers. That fits the comte de Randan, the League governor of Auvergne (killed before Issoire in 1590), and he is the obvious candidate. The key lists “Mr de Randan” as 8, though, and nothing on the leaves names him, so the page calls him a correspondent at Randan. “94, le marquis” in Auvergne that spring is probably the marquis de Canillac, Marguerite’s keeper at Usson, who had gone over to her that winter. That is context, not proof.

Nevers’s file copy of a letter from Saint-Quentin during the siege of Cambrai, with seventeen passages (753 symbols) in a cipher of figures and graphic signs and no contemporary decipherment. Every surviving Nevers key of 1594–95 was tested and none fits. A ciphertext-only solver that recovers a matched control finds no French, so the cipher is not a plain homophonic substitution; not solved without the key. λ χ Ⱡ o 1 9 : 4 1 C π o ∂ m 1 3 T 2 1 2 0 2 2 1 2 0 ħ “pour le regard du […] affin que 72 ne puissent prendre cognoissance de noz affaires” Saint-Quentin → Villeroy · figures and signs, nomenclator · 16 August 1595 The duc de Nevers to Villeroy, 16 August 1595 from Duke of Nevers → to Nicolas de Neufville, seigneur de Villeroy BnF, français 3993, no. 102, ff. 148r–149r: Nevers’s file copy of a letter written from Saint-Quentin while Fuentes besieged Cambrai. Seventeen passages, 753 symbols, are in a cipher of figures and graphic signs. No contemporary decipherment is known. The passages were transcribed from the Gallica scans and tested against every surviving Nevers key of 1594–95; none fits. A ciphertext-only solver recovers the key of a matched control of the same size but finds no French in the letter. The key was not recovered. Daniel Bourdeau · posted 22 September 2026 · updated 26 October 2026 Method: not solved · Extent: text not obtained · On the map not solved At a glance Not solved · text not obtained The letter The duc de Nevers to Villeroy, St Quentin, 16 August 1595, about the relief of Cambrai. It is a clear French copy with seventeen enciphered runs (753 symbols). Where BnF français 3993 f. 148r (Gallica); the catalogue listed it with no known key. The cipher Mostly the figures 1 and 2 with about forty-five graphic signs. Nevers writes the enemy as the code number 72. It is most likely a nomenclator with syllables and code words, not a plain homophonic substitution. How it was tried The closest key in the Nevers collection, no. 76 (fr. 3995 ff. 142v–143r), has the same family of signs but different values and gives no French; nos. 65, 66 and 68–75 do not fit either. A homophonic annealing solver found nothing under six ways of dividing the figures. Why it resists 753 symbols are too few to recover such a key without plaintext. Still open It needs the key (not in fr. 3995) or the letter as Villeroy received it, which may carry his secretary’s decipherment.

f. 148r, the long run: “Or j’ay bien ce mauvais augure…”, three lines of cipher, “par ce qu’il faut necessairement que nous”, three more. Image: Bibliothèque nationale de France, français 3993 f. 148r, via Gallica (btv1b9059229n, view 161). The copy (BnF notice: “Lettre, avec chiffre, de Louis de Gonzague, duc de Nevers, à monseigneur de Villeroy… De St Quentin, ce 16 aoust 1595. Copie”) runs over three pages in a secretary’s hand. Nevers was commanding in Picardy after the fall of Doullens (31 July); Fuentes had opened the siege of Cambrai, held by Balagny, a few days before. The letter is about the relief of Cambrai: a convoy that must risk “ung grand combat”, the people of the town who will not hold, the need to assemble the council. Nevers opens with a reproach that explains the cipher: Vous faictes beaucoup pour le service du Roy a escrire assez intelligiblement … mais il me semble que ce qui est de plus pregnant seroit bon d’estre en chiffre, par ce que s’il se perdoit des lettres … pour le regard du [ cipher ] affin que 72 ne puissent prendre cognoissance de noz affaires. f. 148r l. 7, the first run, between “pour le regard du” and “affin que 72 ne”. Image: Bibliothèque nationale de France, français 3993 f. 148r, via Gallica (btv1b9059229n, view 161). The other runs sit in the same way inside clear sentences: “dans lequel temps il faut se resoudre de […] contre […]” (f. 148v), “et croy que […], pour faire donc telle chose il faut assembler le conseil” (f. 148v), “aussy tost que […]. Et a moy advis” and “et si luy ne parle […], je le doibs declarer” (f. 149r). The copy ends “De St Quentin ce 16. Aoust 1595”.
nevers1595.html#the-cipher

The 753 symbols (measured on the transcription, ct_f148r.txt and ct_f148v_149r.txt ) are of 54 kinds. Figures make up more than half: 1 occurs 112 times, 2 92 times, a small circle (letter o or figure 0; the copy does not distinguish them) 74 times. The figure 1 is followed by another figure 87% of the time and “20” occurs 33 times, so the figures are mostly written in pairs. Cut into pairs wherever a figure is followed by another, only about 45 figures are left over. The other signs are Greek letters (λ, π, θ, Δ, χ, ϖ), ∞, a crossed dagger, a reversed c, a tau, an arch, a u with two bars, and italic letters. There are few repeats longer than four symbols; the longest, “41 0 3 1 2”, occurs twice.

The alphabet of fr. 3995 no. 76 (rotated): a = 8, y, +; b = 7, x; c = 9, z; d = 5, K; e = 3, t, ϖ; … p = λ, h; r = ∂, ƒ, θ; s = □, e, π; nulls at the right. The same family of signs as the letter, with other values. Image: Bibliothèque nationale de France, français 3995 ff. 142v–143r, via Gallica (btv1b525085665, view 274). BnF fr. 3995 is Nevers’s own collection of keys, catalogued by Tomokiyo as nos. 1–76. Those of 1594–95 were opened on the Gallica images: No. 76 (ff. 142v–143r) was transcribed in full. Its alphabet gives each letter a figure, a letter and sometimes a Greek sign (λ, π, θ, Δ, #, ϖ all occur in the letter), eight nulls, and a numbered list of common words in two cycles, dotted numbers 12–99 for A–L and barred 1–100 for M–V, followed by titles, persons, ladies, provinces and towns up to 181. This is the letter’s design, but its values give no French on the runs (1 would be g, 112 times), and 72 is not a party in any of its lists. No. 75 (f. 140v), the “Chiffre commun entre messieurs les secretaires d’estat et messieurs du conseil” given to Nevers, is all figures (A 90–99, E 70–79, I 50–59, O 30–39, U 20–29…), with no signs. No. 66 (ff. 122v–123r) uses λ, π, θ and T, but as n, o, l and r; no. 65 (Lesdiguières, ff. 120v–121r) gives each letter a sign and two numbers between 12 and 64, with 10, 20…100 as nulls. Neither fits. Nos. 68–74 are Italian ciphers or figures only; no. 70 is the Balagny–Charles de Gonzague cipher used at Cambrai in the same weeks, all figures. Balagny’s own letters to Nevers (fr. 3993 ff. 130–134, 245, 255) use another alphabet, reconstructed by Tomokiyo. The key the letter used belonged to the Nevers–Villeroy correspondence and is not among the keys Nevers kept. A “clef d’un chiffre employé par le duc de Nevers” in BnF fr. 3618 ff. 3–4 dates from 1591 and is not digitised.
nevers1595.html#method

A homophonic solver (simulated annealing; one plaintext letter per unit, a five-gram language model of Henri IV’s letters, 600 000 moves, four restarts) was first checked on a control: 753 letters of French in the letter’s seventeen run lengths, enciphered with a random key of 49 homophones and three nulls. It recovers the control’s plaintext letter for letter, and all restarts agree. On the letter it was run under six ways of dividing the figures into units: every sign alone; pairs of figures after 1 or 2; every pair of figures; 1 joined to the following sign (the unit of the 1588 informant’s cipher in the same archive); pairs collapsed to their decade; and no. 65’s design, with 10, 20… as nulls and numbers above 64 as codes. None gives French, and the restarts do not agree with one another. A second solver that lets a unit stand for a consonant-and-vowel syllable, as the figures do in the Court key no. 57, fails on its own control of that design, so that hypothesis cannot be tested at this length.
nevers1595.html#open

All seventeen runs, 753 signs. The key is not in fr. 3995. The letter as sent, in Villeroy’s papers, has not been located; it may carry a decipherment. The transcription is a first pass: the circle is not split into o and 0, and dots over figures (which mark the word cycles in no. 76) are not all recorded. With a key in hand these would be settled on the image. The next letter to Villeroy, from Saint-Quentin on 18 August (fr. 3993 no. 133, ff. 173–174), is all in clear and gives no crib.

Orig. e cifre della Segretaria al nunzio, dal 4 gennaio 1718 al 6 gennaio 1720, ff. 1–403” . The catalogue entry here counted twenty-one, following DECODE’s own grouping, which leaves out the three items dated to 1717 (R172, R174, R176); they are in the same dossier and the same cipher, and all twenty-four are treated together below. The twenty-four items are very unequal. Item 14 alone runs to 9,751 cipher tokens over twenty-one pages; six items are under three hundred tokens, and two are a single short paragraph. nunzio1718.html#system

From Lasry’s key sheet, whose editorial notes state the design outright: The despatch is an undivided stream of digits, with no word division and no group separation. Ordinary elements are two digits ; nomenclator elements are four digits beginning with 4 . Division into groups is therefore deterministic: a 4 opens a four-digit group, anything else is a pair. The single digit 3 is a null , except when it falls among the three digits after a 4 prefix, where it belongs to the nomenclator group and is not a null. This is the one place the scheme is not context-free, and Lasry flags it. Homophony is modest for letters and heavy for punctuation: 50 alone for a , 17|71 for i , 12|21 for c , but six variants for the full stop ( 303|323|343|363|373|393 ). A few two-digit groups are syllables or short words rather than letters: 91|94 = che , 55 = con , 78|88 = del , 01 = al . The nomenclator is a series of runs, each ordered alphabetically within itself, and this is what makes the missing values recoverable: range contents 4001–4078 particles, pronouns and word endings, loosely alphabetical ( ancora, ben, come, essere, fare, molto, quando, quanto, questo, tutto, -zione ) 4079–4296 nouns, titles and names, A–R ( Arcivescovo, Armi, Auditore, Camera, Capitolo, Chiesa, Concistoro, Corte, Ecclesiastica, Guerra, Imperatore, Italia, Napoli, Pace, Regni, Religione ) 4401–4479 the same alphabet continued, S–V ( risoluzione, Roma, S. Sede, scrittura, sempre, Sig.re, Spagna, spedizione, subito, tempo, troppo, Turco, Ungheria, Vienna ) 4485–4531 calendar words and the day numbers, 4501–4531 = 01–31 in plain order 4532–4543, 4552–4563 two parallel month runs, Gennaio to Dicembre (see below) 4564–4619 a second alphabetical run, A–T ( aggiustamento, alcun, altro, attenzione, Breve, conforme, costì, dispaccio, giustizia, parola, possibile, pubblico, riflessione, stesso, tempi ) 4681, 4706, 4870+ scattered later blocks ( Cristian-, contro, espulsione, present- )

nunzio1718.html#method

No cryptanalysis was needed and none was done. The method has two halves, and a value was only accepted when both agreed, or when one of them was overwhelming on its own. The bracket. Because each run is alphabetical, a group without a value lies between its nearest neighbours that have one. 4467 sits between 4466 troppo and 4468 Turco , so it begins tr… to tu… . 4198 sits between 4197 maggior and 4200 necessari . 4233 sits between 4231 occasione and the opportun­ recovered at 4236, so it is of… . The contexts. The corpus is 84,961 tokens with everything else already decrypted, so each group without a value comes with its sentences. 4467 appears in “far retrocedere le numerose — che si dicono già incamminate” and “presi nelle proprie case con — di fanteria”. Both halves give truppe . The agreement of the two is the check. 4469 lies between Turco and Vescovo , so it is va–ve ; its contexts are “li — di Spagna hanno preso camino”, “il soccorso de’ — da mandarsi in Levante” and a list of “due palandre et undici barche”. Vascelli satisfies both and nothing else does. The calendar block, and the control it supplies. The month codes were recovered together, as a structure. Lasry’s sheet has only three of them: 4535 “Apte” , 4539 Agosto , 4562 Novembre . The corpus uses 4533 to 4539 contiguously and 4560 to 4562, always after a day number and before passato or corrente . Two parallel Gennaio–Dicembre runs at 4532–4543 and 4552–4563 place Agosto at 4539 and Novembre at 4562 exactly, and make Lasry’s “Apte” Aprile , the fourth slot. That scheme puts Luglio at 4538, and one sentence of the corpus confirms 4538 = Luglio . The corpus has “in data delli 4499 4538 passato, qual appunto fu il giorno della promozione del Sig. Card.” Giulio Alberoni was created cardinal by Clement XI on 12 July 1717 . The month run, derived from an offset, lands on Luglio; the day code beside it is 12; and the sentence names the day of the promotion. Three independent things agree, and 4499 = 12 follows.

These are Clement XI’s Secretariat writing to the nuncio at Madrid in the two years when relations with Philip V collapsed: Alberoni’s Sardinian and Sicilian expeditions, the Quadruple Alliance, and Spain’s retaliation against the Roman jurisdiction. Two words run through everything and both of them were among the groups without a value, which shows what the gap in the key cost. The first is promozione , the 45-token group: whether Rome would make the promotion Alberoni wanted, and whether it should be held back as leverage. The second is aggiustamento , the settlement of the “note pendenze”: the giurisdizione , the tribunale of the nunciature in Spain, the abolition of the Nunziatura at Naples, the espulsione of the nuncio. Around them run the vascelli of Spain taking their course for the Levante, the Emperor’s truppe in the Ferrarese, the Turco , and the Trattato of the neutrality of Italy. A specimen from the reading of 364D/3 ( lasry/R156_reading.md ). The Secretariat writes on the Spanish ambassador at Rome, Cardinal Acquaviva: … il Sig. Card. Acquaviva, a cui non solo per mezzo mio ma da se stesso ancora procurò N.S. di far conoscere l’indispensabile necessità di tal sospensione, non mostrando d’appagarsene, pretese di rimuoverne N.S. con dedurre le sue ragioni compilate nella scrittura di cui, non con altra mira, se le manda copia che per far vedere costì la loro insussistenza e la stranezza delle massime con le quali si sostengono…

The recurring business is the promotion of Cardinal Alberoni and the settlement of the pending disputes between Rome and Spain: the nuncio's jurisdiction, the abolition of the Nunziatura in Naples, the expulsion of the nuncio, the Spanish ships bound for the Levant, the Emperor, the Turk and the peace treaty. L'espulsione del Nunzio da Napoli e l'abolizione totale di ogni vestigio di autorità Apostolica in quel Regno è stata seguitata dall'interdirsi al Nunzio di Vienna l'accesso alla Corte et ogni commercio con quei Ministri, minacciandosi molto più se il Papa non smentisse con fatti la detta calunnia. Da questo poco raccolga Vostra Signoria Illustrissima lo stato in cui si trova la Santità Sua. Speravasi che la pietà di cotesto Re, conoscendo la giustizia delle doglianze e l'equità delle insinuazioni di Sua Santità, fosse per risolversi alla restituzione della Sardegna et a rimettere le cose nel pristino stato; ma non si è nemmeno compiaciuta la Maestà Sua di rispondere al Breve de 25 di Agosto, con il quale Sua Santità le ne faceva premurosissime istanze. Anzi si ode da tutte le parti che ad altro non si pensi costì che ad ammassar truppe, a fabricar navi et a disporsi alla continuazione della guerra, di che le lettere di Barcellona, di Alicante e di Cadice istruiscono tutto il mondo. Fra tante disgrazie è sensibilissimo a Sua Santità che Vostra Signoria Illustrissima non scriva una parola di tanti apparati, i quali, avendo allarmati tutti gli altri Ministri, è impossibile che a Lei solamente siano tuttavia ignoti; e che invece di sentirsi da Lei qualche frutto delle paterne rimostranze del Papa per la restituzione della Sardegna, si oda da altri che si prendano costì tutte le misure per far nuove conquiste. Un tal pensiero ferisce il cuore di Nostro Signore, tanto più che il silenzio di Vostra Signoria Illustrissima si stende ancora a tutte le altre cose più importanti del suo Ministero. Nulla si è saputo fin'ora se il Concordato della forma che stà del Breve di ratifica sia stato confermato dal Re. Nulla se la Maestà Sua sia stata assoluta, in vigore delle facoltà datene al Padre Daubenton, dalle censure incorse. Nulla se e come abbia fatta la consaputa composizione co' Regii Ministri sopra li spogli e frutti delle vacanti indebitamente percetti. Nulla se sia stato eletto secondo il solito il nuovo Agente delle Chiese, e quando sia per portarsi a risiedere in questa Corte. Nulla finalmente dell'enorme violazione dell'Immunità Ecclesiastica occorsi ne' già scritti fatti di Valenza e di Toledo. È in sostanza ridotto il Papa a sapere solo dalle publiche gazette, o da particolari, quelle notizie che sì strettamente riguardano il Ministerio del Nunzio Apostolico. Quale ragione possa Ella addurre per suo scarico io non lo so. So bene che un tal silenzio tiene in angustia la Santità Sua, e nell'essere all'oscuro delle necessarie notizie non sa come regolarsi in sì gravi circostanze la sua condotta. Due cose principalmente danno corso alle indegne voci sparse contro la lealtà Pontificia. La prima, che il Breve scritto al Re Cattolico sotto li 25 d'Agosto non sia stato presentato al Re. La seconda, che li Brevi spettanti li due noti sussidii sopra li beni ecclesiastici dell'Indie e della Spagna abbiano almeno indirettamente la loro esecuzione. Quanto alla prima, perché non ha Ella vivamente rappresentato e fatto rappresentare alla Maestà Sua il debito che le correva, e sempre più le corre, di rispondere al detto Breve, particolarmente in queste circostanze, in cui il non farlo priva il Papa di un'arme potentissima per confondere tanti calunniatori e difendere il suo decoro sì altamente oltraggiato? Quanto alla seconda, è impercettibile come non si ottenga che li sudetti due Brevi ritornino nelle nostre mani, mentre, essendo questi di loro natura inesequibili, non la mutano per restare nelle mani del Re, né divengono in alcun modo esequibili; anzi che, se la Maestà Sua volesse farne qualche uso, non potrebbe Sua Santità per debito di coscienza dispensarsi dal rivocarli espressamente; e quando anche volesse il Papa gratificare in altro tempo la Maestà Sua di somiglianti sussidii, sarebbe necessaria la spedizione di nuovi Brevi. Come dunque può ragionevolmente ciò negarsi al Papa? Quando l'essere li Brevi nelle mani del Re non gli giova, et il non essere nelle nostre ci porta un essenziale pregiudizio, per mancarci un incontrastabile documento da giustificare al mondo che in realtà questi Brevi non si eseguiscono. Se almeno ci avesse Ella mandate sopra di ciò autentiche attestazioni de' Vescovi et Capitoli di Spagna, o almeno dell'Arcivescovo e Capitolo di cotesta Metropolitana di Toledo, averessimo qualche mezzo per provare la verità di un fatto per altro sì contrastato; ma queste ancora ci mancano. Che cosa dunque deve fare Vostra Signoria Illustrissima? Deve ben ponderare l'infelice stato in cui è ridotto Nostro Signore, e essere persuasa che, se alla sua efficacia non riuscirà di conseguire costì i mezzi per liberarnelo, non potrà fare a meno Sua Santità di ricorrere a quelli che stimerà necessarii per scancellare dalla mente degli uomini gli indegni sospetti concepiti contro il Vicario di Cristo. ## Notes - Alignment (lasry/R154_align.tsv, R154_words.tsv; research/reading_audit/b22_nunzio_align.py): 4,030 letters of the decipherment; 2,998 carried by a group's own value, 430 by nomenclator codes whose value is the decipherer's word or its abbreviation, 93 (2.3%) by a two- or four-figure group read as its look-alike (1/7, 0/6, 0/9 ...), 255 on groups DECODE marks unread ('NN?'), 163 where the group gives other letters (mostly code 4261 rendered 'il Papa' / 'Sua Santità', and drift around DECODE's mis-split figures), 91 without a group (doubled consonants the cipher spells single). Same holes as the reading (there are none). --> # R154, the Secretariat of State to the nuncio in Madrid, Rome, 11 January 1718 (Spagna 364D/1) ## Translation Our Lord's troubles grow on hearing that the horrid calumny is gaining ever more strength, that the Vicar of Christ was an accomplice in the baneful wrong done by the King of Spain to Christendom and to His Holiness, and on seeing its most pernicious effects. The expulsion of the nuncio from Naples and the total abolition of every vestige of Apostolic authority in that kingdom has been followed by the nuncio in Vienna being forbidden access to the court and all dealings with those ministers, with much more threatened if the Pope does not refute the said calumny with deeds. From this little, Your Most Illustrious Lordship may gather the state in which His Holiness finds himself. It was hoped that the piety of the King there, recognising the justice of the complaints and the fairness of His Holiness's suggestions, would resolve to restore Sardinia and to put things back as they were; but His Majesty has not even deigned to answer the Brief of 25 August in which His Holiness made most pressing requests to him for it. On the contrary, one hears from every side that nothing else is thought of there but massing troops, building ships and preparing to continue the war, of which the letters from Barcelona, Alicante and Cadiz are informing the whole world. Among so many misfortunes it is most painful to His Holiness that Your Most Illustrious Lordship does not write a word about so many preparations, which, having alarmed all the other ministers, cannot possibly be unknown to you alone; and that instead of hearing from you some fruit of the Pope's fatherly remonstrances for the restitution of Sardinia, one hears from others that every measure is being taken there for new conquests. Such a thought wounds Our Lord's heart, all the more because your silence extends also to all the other more important matters of your ministry. Nothing has been learned so far as to whether the Concordat, in the form set out in the Brief of ratification, has been confirmed by the King. Nothing as to whether His Majesty has been absolved from the censures incurred, by virtue of the faculties given for it to Father Daubenton. Nothing as to whether, and how, he has made the agreed composition with the royal ministers over the spolia and the revenues of vacant sees unduly collected. Nothing as to whether the new Agent of the Churches has been elected as usual, and when he is to come and reside at this court. Nothing, finally, about the enormous violation of ecclesiastical immunity that occurred in the incidents already reported at Valencia and Toledo. The Pope is in substance reduced to learning only from the public gazettes, or from private persons, news that so closely concerns the ministry of the Apostolic Nuncio. What reason you can offer in your defence I do not know. I know well that such a silence keeps His Holiness in distress, and that, being in the dark about the necessary news, he does not know how to regulate his conduct in such grave circumstances. Two things chiefly give currency to the shameful rumours spread against the Pontiff's good faith. The first, that the Brief written to the Catholic King on 25 August has not been presented to the King. The second, that the Briefs concerning the two well-known subsidies on the ecclesiastical property of the Indies and of Spain are, at least indirectly, being put into effect. As to the first: why have you not forcefully represented, and had represented, to His Majesty the duty he was under, and is more and more under, to reply to the said Brief, particularly in the present circumstances, in which not doing so deprives the Pope of a most powerful weapon for confounding so many slanderers and defending his honour, so grievously outraged? As to the second, it is incomprehensible that you cannot obtain the return of the said two Briefs to our hands, since, being unenforceable by their nature, they do not change it by remaining in the King's hands, nor do they become in any way enforceable; indeed, if His Majesty wished to make any use of them, His Holiness could not in conscience refrain from expressly revoking them; and even if the Pope wished at another time to favour His Majesty with similar subsidies, new Briefs would have to be issued. How then can this reasonably be denied to the Pope? When the Briefs being in the King's hands does him no good, while their not being in ours does us essential harm, because we lack an incontestable document with which to show the world that these Briefs are in reality not being executed. If at least you had sent us authentic attestations of this from the bishops and chapters of Spain, or at least from the Archbishop and Chapter of the metropolitan church of Toledo, we would have some means of proving the truth of a fact otherwise so disputed; but these too are lacking. What then must Your Most Illustrious Lordship do? You must weigh well the unhappy state to which Our Lord is reduced, and be persuaded that if your efforts do not succeed in obtaining there the means to free him from it, His Holiness will not be able to avoid resorting to those he judges necessary to erase from men's minds the shameful suspicions conceived against the Vicar of Christ. Ill.ma il rammarico di N.S. per sapere che, nonostante il primo Capitolo del noto Concordato, si continuava costì come prima ad opprimere l'autorità et a violare l'immunità Ecclesiastica; e le ho ancora espresso lo stupore di N.S. per non riceversi da Lei alcun riscontro de' strepitosi particolari attentati che in tal proposito si andavano ogni giorno cumulando da' Regii Ministri. Ma non mi è mai occorso di dover espressamente dolermi del suo contegno, come sono costretto di fare ora che Ella mi tace uno de' maggiori eccessi che possa commettere la podestà laicale contro l'Ecclesiastica, e di cui abbiamo pur troppo in mano documenti autentici et irrefragabili. Si è questo l'espulsione del Vescovo di Vich e l'ordine dato da' Regii Ministri, il che vuol dire in sostanza da chi presentemente è l'arbitro di cotesto governo, a quel Capitolo di procedere all'elezione di un Vicario Capitolare, come se la Chiesa fosse vacante, che pure da sei anni in qua incirca è piena. Il tutto è seguito fin da 29 d'Ottobre passato, cioè a dire un mese e mezzo prima della data delle sue ultime lettere, tempo assai lungo per potere Ella essere ragguagliata di un sì strano successo e per potercene dare un cenno. Quali siano per essere le risoluzioni di N.S. io non lo so; so ben che le prenderà tali da far conoscere al mondo che non è capace di soffrire simili procedure senza risentirsene et esigerne la dovuta riparazione. ## Notes - Line 1: Lasry's group gives 'stessi' where the interlinear has 'volte'; line 5 the figures are garbled ('an e s r giustizia') where the interlinear has 'ancora espresso lo'; line 6 'fdelc' before 'stupore' unread. N.S. = Nostro Signore, Our Lord (the Pope). --> # R155, the Secretariat of State to the nuncio in Madrid, Rome, 18 January 1718 (Spagna 364D/2, f. 24r-v): English translation ## Translation I have several times made known to Your Most Illustrious Lordship Our Lord's regret at learning that, notwithstanding the first chapter of the well-known Concordat, the authority and the immunity of the Church continued to be oppressed and violated there as before; and I have also expressed to you Our Lord's astonishment at receiving from you no account of the notorious particular outrages which the Royal Ministers were heaping up every day in this regard. But it has never happened that I had expressly to complain of your conduct, as I am forced to do now that you are silent to me about one of the greatest excesses that the lay power can commit against the ecclesiastical, and of which we have, alas, authentic and irrefutable documents in hand. This is the expulsion of the Bishop of Vich, and the order given by the Royal Ministers, which means in substance by whoever is at present the arbiter of that government, to that Chapter to proceed to the election of a Capitular Vicar, as if the see were vacant, when it has in fact been filled for about six years now. The whole took place as long ago as the 29th of October last, that is to say a month and a half before the date of your last letters, a time quite long enough for you to be informed of so strange an event and to give us a hint of it. What Our Lord's resolutions are to be, I do not know; I know well that he will take such as to make the world know that he is not capable of suffering such proceedings without resenting them and exacting the due reparation. Ill.ma sotto li 25 del caduto i motivi che costringevano N.S. a sospendere al Sig. Card. Alberoni la grazia della traslazione alla Chiesa di Siviglia sin a tanto che sopra di essi non fosse restata pienamente sodisfatta la Santità Sua. Ora devo parteciparle che il Sig. Card. Acquaviva, a cui non solo per mezzo mio ma da se stesso ancora procurò N.S. di far conoscere l'indispensabile necessità di tal sospensione, non mostrando d'appagarsene, pretese di rimuoverne N.S. con dedurre le sue ragioni compilate nella scrittura di cui, non con altra mira, se le manda copia che per far vedere costì la loro insussistenza e la stranezza delle massime con le quali si sostengono da S. Em.za i pretesi diritti del Re. Io stimo superfluo d'indicarle a V.S. Ill.ma, perché la sola lettura di questi fogli basterà per farle conoscere il veleno che contengono, et in specie ove impudentemente si asserisce nulla e destituta di ogni titolo legitimo la provista del Vescovato di Vich nella persona di chi con autorità Apostolica è vero e solo Vescovo di quella Chiesa, e per tale è stato riconosciuto per sei e più anni, ne' quali senza alcun disturbo o contradizione della potestà laicale ne ha goduto il possesso pacifico; non potendosi dire se non con manifesto errore da verun Cattolico che l'instituzione de' Vescovi dipenda o possa dipendere da qualunque altra autorità che da quella data da Cristo alla sua Chiesa. Come può ben credere V.S. Ill.ma, non fece nell'animo di N.S. alcuna forza la sudetta scrittura, capace solo d'esacerbarlo e d'alienarlo dal condescendere a ciò che in sostanza non è altro che una pura e mera grazia. Ma la cosa non si è fermata qui; poiché, essendosi il Sig. Card. Acquaviva senza alcun fondamento lusingato che dovesse N.S. differire il Concistoro sino al ritorno delle risposte di costì, nell'avere poi udito che non poteva la Santità Sua ritardarlo per proporvi la Chiesa di Nanchino, perché altrimente le Bolle non potrebbono giungere in Portogallo avanti che le navi destinate alla Cina sarpassero da Lisbona, ha aggiunto alle strane proposizioni avanzate nel foglio sudetto varie minaccie di rotture e di proteste; quasi che il diritto che hanno i Re Cattolici a presentare i soggetti per le Chiese di Spagna si stendesse alle traslazioni d'una Chiesa all'altra, e che non ne potesse il Papa, senza lesione delle regie prerogative, differire l'effettuazione per uno et anco più Concistori, siccome è stato solito di praticarsi in ogni paese Cattolico e con tutti i Principi indifferentemente, non solo circa le traslazioni, ove non ha luogo né nomina né presentazione, ma ancora circa le semplici proviste delle Chiese, ove s'ammette l'una e l'altra. Il Papa, benché potesse farlo, non nega di fare la sudetta traslazione, ma la differisce finché resti sincerato sopra le scandalose novità occorse dopo l'intenzione datane già al Sig. Card. Acquaviva, e sia per conseguenza in grado di poterla fare senza aggravio della propria coscienza e senza dare un pernicioso esempio. Se questo moderatissimo contegno merita di essere corrisposto con sentimenti espressi nella prefata scrittura, e con le publiche dichiarazioni alle quali si prepara il Sig. Card. Acquaviva, anche con chiamare a causa gli altri Principi, come apparisce dal tenore del viglietto scritto da S. Em.za a Mons. [?Segretario] del Concistoro, di cui le aggiungo pur copia, io mi rimetto a chiunque ha qualche senso di giustizia e di equità. So bene che, quantunque sia ormai abituato N.S. in 18 anni di spinosissimo Pontificato a veder per lo più rivoltati contro questa S. Sede quelli stessi che da Lei sono stati più distintamente beneficati, non può tuttavia imaginarsi mai che il Sig. Card. Alberoni, la cui promozione costa tanto a N.S., voglia seguirne l'esempio con sostenere l'impegno preso senza alcun colore, non che titolo di ragione, dal Sig. Card. Acquaviva, e non debba piuttosto procurare con la sua autorità e prudenza di toglier di mezzo quelli ostacoli che unicamente gli ritardano il conseguimento della desiderata traslazione. A questo oggetto devono tendere tutte le premure di V.S. Ill.ma, e non dubito che Ella ve l'impiegherà con tutta la maggior efficacia. Dopo scritto fin qui il Sig. Card. Acquaviva ha con un viglietto replicate le istanze a N.S. perché si degnasse di far differire il Concistoro già destinato per venerdì prossimo. Si sarebbe forse la Santità Sua indotta a compiacerlo, quando la proposizione della Chiesa di Nanchino non patisse la minima dilazione; ma sappia V.S. Ill.ma che, anco proponendosi venerdì, appena le Bolle giungeranno in tempo a Lisbona. Consideri ciò che sarebbe se si framettesse maggior indugio. N.S., giaché non ha potuto consolare quel Re con l'erezione di nuovi Vescovati nella Cina, quantunque le suppliche e le istanze sieno state lunghissime et efficacissime, non può ritardargli di vantaggio, dopo reiterati impegni, la provista di quello già eretto; tanto più che, essendo pur troppo la Maestà Sua per questo capo molto mal contenta di noi, e [?per ciò] già comincia a mettere in dubio la trasmissione delle navi in Levante per quest'anno, che pure è l'unico aiuto che possiamo sperare, non vuole N.S. darle nuovo motivo di negare alla Christianità un soccorso sì necessario, et esser egli debitore presso il mondo tutto di un sì grave comune pregiudizio. Del resto torno a dire a V.S. Ill.ma che la Santità Sua è pronta a proporre la Chiesa di Siviglia subito che sarà sodisfatta sopra li punti consaputi. Oltre li grandi e gravi attentati contro l'autorità Ecclesiastica commessi dalla potestà laicale in cotesto Regno, de' quali, senza aversene da V.S. Ill.ma alcun lume, le sono andato di mano in mano esprimendo le giustissime doglianze di N.S., si è qua avuto riscontro che, non contenti i Regii Ministri d'avere con la nota violenza espulso il Vicario di Valenza, siensi anco avanzati a destinare di propria autorità per amministratore di quella Chiesa il Vescovo di Burgos. È stato ciò udito da N.S. con orrore insieme et ammirazione, tanto più che V.S. Ill.ma non mi dice parola di un tal eccesso, e molto meno di averne procurato il necessario riparo, giaché N.S. non può in alcun modo soffrire, senza mancare al proprio debito, che alcuno s'ingerisca nell'amministrazione e governo di una Chiesa senza essere fornito di ... ## Notes - Two despatches of 8 February 1718 are on the record: the first (ff. 47r-50v) and the beginning of a second (f. 51r); the cipher of the second stops at the foot of f. 51r ('fornito di', the rest not in this record). - Where the figures are garbled the interlinear is followed: f. 47v 'del Vescovato di Vich' (figures 'ce [4720] [?]'); 'pura e mera grazia'; 'contenti' / 'contenta' (Lasry's 4113 'Card.le' stands where the sense and the interlinear need 'conte-'); 'si è qua avuto riscontro' (figures 'tanto [4603]'); 'sentimenti' (figures 'rii'). Now I must inform you that Cardinal Acquaviva, to whom Our Lord took care to make known the indispensable necessity of such a suspension, not only through me but also by himself, not showing himself satisfied with it, claimed to move Our Lord from it by setting out his reasons, compiled in the writing of which a copy is sent to you for no other purpose than to show there their lack of substance and the strangeness of the maxims with which His Eminence upholds the alleged rights of the King. I think it superfluous to point them out to Your Most Illustrious Lordship, because the mere reading of these sheets will suffice to make you know the poison they contain, and in particular where it is impudently asserted that the provision of the bishopric of Vich, in the person of him who by Apostolic authority is the true and only Bishop of that Church, is void and destitute of any lawful title, and who has been recognised as such for six years and more, during which he has enjoyed peaceful possession of it without any disturbance or contradiction from the lay power; since no Catholic can say, except by manifest error, that the institution of bishops depends, or can depend, on any authority other than that given by Christ to His Church. As Your Most Illustrious Lordship may well believe, the aforesaid writing made no impression on Our Lord's mind, capable only of embittering him and turning him away from granting what in substance is nothing but a pure and simple grace. But the matter has not stopped there; for Cardinal Acquaviva, having flattered himself without any foundation that Our Lord was to put off the Consistory until the return of the answers from there, on hearing that His Holiness could not delay it, because the Church of Nanking was to be proposed in it, since otherwise the Bulls could not reach Portugal before the ships bound for China sailed from Lisbon, has added to the strange propositions put forward in the said sheet various threats of ruptures and protests; as if the right the Catholic Kings have to present persons for the Churches of Spain extended to translations from one Church to another, and as if the Pope could not, without injury to the royal prerogatives, defer carrying it out for one or even more Consistories, as has been the custom in every Catholic country and with all princes alike, not only in translations, where there is neither nomination nor presentation, but also in the simple provisions of Churches, where both are admitted. The Pope, though he could do so, does not refuse to make the said translation, but defers it until he is reassured about the scandalous innovations that occurred after the intention of it had already been given to Cardinal Acquaviva, and is consequently in a position to make it without burdening his own conscience and without setting a pernicious example. Whether this most moderate conduct deserves to be answered with sentiments such as are expressed in the aforesaid writing, and with the public declarations for which Cardinal Acquaviva is preparing, even calling the other princes into the cause, as appears from the tenor of the note written by His Eminence to Monsignor the [?Secretary] of the Consistory, of which I also add a copy, I leave to anyone who has some sense of justice and equity. I know well that, although Our Lord is by now accustomed, in eighteen years of a most thorny pontificate, to see turned against this Holy See for the most part those very persons whom it has most distinctly benefited, he can nevertheless never imagine that Cardinal Alberoni, whose promotion cost Our Lord so much, should wish to follow their example by upholding the position taken by Cardinal Acquaviva without any colour, let alone title, of reason, and should not rather try with his authority and prudence to remove those obstacles which alone delay his obtaining the desired translation. To this object all Your Most Illustrious Lordship's efforts must tend, and I do not doubt that you will employ them there with all the greatest effectiveness. After writing thus far, Cardinal Acquaviva has repeated his instances to Our Lord in a note, that he would deign to have the Consistory already fixed for next Friday put off. His Holiness would perhaps have been induced to oblige him, if the proposal of the Church of Nanking did not suffer the least delay; but let Your Most Illustrious Lordship know that, even if it is proposed on Friday, the Bulls will barely reach Lisbon in time. Consider what it would be if a longer delay were interposed. Our Lord, since he has not been able to console that King with the erection of new bishoprics in China, although the petitions and instances have been very long and very pressing, cannot delay any further for him, after repeated engagements, the provision of the one already erected; all the more as, His Majesty being, alas, much displeased with us on this head, and [?therefore] already beginning to call into doubt the sending of the ships to the Levant this year, which is yet the only help we can hope for, Our Lord does not wish to give him a new reason to deny Christendom so necessary a succour, and himself to be answerable before the whole world for so grave a common prejudice. For the rest, I say again to Your Most Illustrious Lordship that His Holiness is ready to propose the Church of Seville as soon as he is satisfied on the points you know of. Besides the great and grave outrages against ecclesiastical authority committed by the lay power in that kingdom, of which, without having had any light from Your Most Illustrious Lordship, I have gone on expressing to you one by one Our Lord's most just complaints, we have had word here that the Royal Ministers, not content with having expelled the Vicar of Valencia with the well-known violence, have even gone so far as to appoint on their own authority the Bishop of Burgos as administrator of that Church. Our Lord heard this with horror and wonder together, all the more since Your Most Illustrious Lordship does not say a word to me of such an excess, and much less of having procured the necessary remedy for it, since Our Lord can in no way suffer, without failing in his own duty, that anyone should meddle in the administration and government of a Church without being furnished with ... Ill.ma da' congiunti fogli la condotta tenuta dal Sig. Card. Acquaviva per essersi da N.S. non già negata ma semplicemente differita la proposizione della Chiesa di Siviglia, e le parti fatte da' Ministri di N.S. per pura e mera [?preservazione] delle incontrastabili ragioni che assistono alla S. Sede et alla Santità Sua in questo negozio. Tre cose, oltre alla protesta, hanno giustamente accresciuta l'amarezza di N.S., il quale spera che neanco potranno essere in alcun modo approvate dal Re. La prima consta dal foglio segnato A. Basta leggerlo per convenire della strana pretensione di Mons. Herrera, quasi che dovesse esser libero a' Regii Ministri il difendere nella maniera che più lor piace le pretese insussistenti reali prerogative per aggravare il Papa, et all'incontro fosse a' Ministri di N.S. impedito di sostenere le proprie fortissime et irrefragabili ragioni con quelli atti che sono proprii a preservarle. Il rispondere alle proteste è una difesa concessa ad ognuno, e stile inconcusso fra tutte le nazioni, e praticata ancora dal Sig. Card. Corradini nel millesettecento dieci, quando era Auditore, come apparisce dal foglio segnato lettera B; et è bensì grazia e favore l'essere il Papa permesso che da' suoi stessi Ministri si ricevesse quella fatta per parte del Sig. Card. Acquaviva nel caso presente, in cui, per non inferirsi alcun pregiudizio a' diritti del Re, come diffusamente scrissi a V.S. Ill.ma con il passato dispaccio, poteva senza alcun torto né ingiuria rigettarsi. La seconda riguarda li quattro motivi addotti nell'atto di protesta che si manda segnata lettera C, fatta da Mons. Herrera in nome del Sig. Card. Acquaviva per Mons. Auditore di N.S., e poi eseguita in Cancellaria e registrata in quel tribunale. Quattro se ne arrecano. È falso in primo luogo che mai siensi differite le proposizioni delle Chiese alle quali hanno li Principi il diritto di nomina o di presentazione; e ne sono molti esempii, bastando veder gli atti del Concistoro per restarne convinto. Per le traslazioni poi tanto è falso ciò che si asserisce, che ne' Pontificati antecedenti se ne esaminavano le cause nella Congregazione Concistoriale, ove, quando quelle non erano canoniche, si rigettavano le traslazioni; che se da qualche tempo in qua si è in parte rilasciato il rigore praticato prima circa la verificazione delle cause sudette, il che però non è stato sempre, non è già per questo che siensi correntemente e quasi alla cieca ammesse, ove non solo mancassero i requisiti prescritti da' sacri Canoni, ne concorressero circostanze totalmente opposte alla concessione della grazia richiesta, come nel caso nostro. Secondariamente non s'intende in qual pregiudizio del regio diritto cada questa dilazione, la quale dipende dall'arbitrio di cotesta Corte; mentre, se il Papa sarà sodisfatto sopra li punti consaputi, o almeno circa l'espulsione del Vescovo di Vich e l'amministrazione delle rendite della mensa di Tarragona, è disposto, nonostante la condotta che qui si tiene da' Regii Ministri, a troncare ogni indugio. Lo scandalo poi che si adduce in terzo luogo risulterebbe piuttosto in Spagna dal vedersi che il Papa, senza avere alcun riguardo alle consapute gravissime novità sì lesive di ogni autorità Ecclesiastica, e prima di riportarne il dovuto riparo, facesse quelle grazie che appena farebbe quando la potestà laicale non strapazzasse ma rispettasse l'Ecclesiastica, e non si ingerisse in quelle cose che per ogni diritto a lei sola appartengono. Al quarto motivo finalmente è abbastanza risposto nella controprotesta che si manda segnata lettera D, fatta similmente registrare da Mons. Auditore negli atti della Cancellaria; al che devo solo aggiungere che N.S. pensa di disporre talmente de' frutti della Chiesa di Siviglia in questo tempo di vacanza, che nessuno potrà dolersi ch'egli li abbia applicati ad uso contrario a' sacri Canoni, e molto meno ch'egli ne abbia voluto impinguare la Camera Apostolica. La terza concerne la divulgazione che fin con le stampe, et anco con la traduzione in Italiano, come apparisce dall'esemplare annesso che le trasmetto, ha fatto della detta protesta il Sig. Card. Acquaviva. È veramente restato sorpreso il Papa ad un tal passo, parendogli di avere proceduto in modo da non dover essere corrisposto con tali publicità. Sa l'Em.za Sua con quanta amarezza, e solamente costretto dal proprio debito, abbia N.S. sospesa la proposizione della Chiesa di Siviglia. Sa che la Santità Sua differì sin a venerdì il Concistoro per aspettare l'ordinario di Spagna, sperando di poter riavere con esso qualche notizia che l'avesse posta in grado di venire alla sudetta proposizione. Sa inoltre la disposizione nella quale si trovava la Santità Sua a ritardare il Concistoro, nonostante che tre esami de' Vescovi fossero preceduti, quando la provista della Chiesa di Nanchin non l'avesse violentata per le ragioni già scritte con la passata cifra. Sopra la detta divulgazione non mi sono note le risoluzioni che prenderà la Santità Sua per indennità delle sue ragioni e di quelle della S. Sede. Mi è ben noto il sommo pregiudizio che fin nella propria estimazione e decoro presso le nazioni straniere è derivato a N.S. dalle troppo cautelate e circospette misure guardate unicamente per non dispiacere al Re di Spagna circa la divulgazione dell'orrenda mancanza fattagli l'anno scorso; e mi è altresì noto trovarsi in potere di N.S. una quantità di biglietti scritti di proprio pugno dal Sig. Card. Acquaviva, co' quali, e con uno in specie de' cinque Agosto, assicurava N.S. che le navi erano partite et incaminate in aiuto dell'Armata Cristiana in Levante. Tutte queste notizie e ponderazioni, che si accennano a V.S. Ill.ma per sua istruzione e per valersene opportunamente, fanno sperare al Papa che il Re Cattolico, conoscendo le rettissime intenzioni di N.S., vorrà ben prendere in buona parte l'indispensabile necessità in cui è stata la Santità Sua di dover sospendere la proposizione della Chiesa sudetta, e l'ecciteranno a somministrare al Papa i mezzi perché possano essere appagate le sue regie istanze. ## Notes - Lasry's open groups read from the interlinear: 4389 'La' (three places: la prima, la seconda, la terza), 4497 'dieci' ('millesettecento dieci'), 4358 'È' (before 'falso'), 4381 'Lo' (before 'scandalo'), 4301 'Al', 4237 'ordinario', 4340 'Tutte queste notizie' (with the next group). 4201 'Santità Sua' (key_b22 review value) fits ('prenderà la Santità Sua').
